title: Top 10 Global Fabless IC Design Houses Post 73% YoY Revenue Growth in 2Q26 Says TrendForce
gist: TrendForce data shows the top 10 fabless chip designers generated $141.45B in Q2 2026 revenue, up 73% YoY, with Nvidia at $91.16B (64% share) and Broadcom and AMD posting even faster growth as AI spending broadens beyond GPUs to CPUs, custom silicon, networking and power management, while smartphone-exposed vendors like Qualcomm lag.

insights.claim: The world's 10 largest fabless chip designers generated more than $141.45 billion in combined revenue in Q2 2026, up 73% year over year, according to TrendForce.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Confirms AI capex is still accelerating fabless industry revenue at triple-digit-adjacent rates well into 2026, a leading indicator for foundry and equipment demand.
insights.locator: The world's 10 largest fabless chip designers generated more than $141.45 billion

insights.claim: AI spending is reshaping the semiconductor hierarchy by lifting suppliers of GPUs, CPUs, custom accelerators and high-speed networking while leaving smartphone-focused vendors under pressure.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Investors should rotate exposure toward data-center/AI-infrastructure-linked fabless names and away from smartphone-cycle-dependent ones.
insights.locator: The surge underscores how artificial intelligence spending

insights.claim: The AI boom is expanding beyond graphics processors, with value shifting toward the full compute stack spanning CPUs, custom accelerators, networking, power management and optical links.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Signals broadening AI capex beneficiaries beyond Nvidia GPUs into adjacent silicon categories, widening the investable AI-infrastructure universe.
insights.quote: The results show that the AI boom is expanding beyond graphics processors. Value is shifting toward an entire compute stack spanning CPUs, custom accelerators, networking, power management and optical links.
insights.locator: Bottom line: The results show that the AI boom

insights.claim: Nvidia remained the dominant fabless player with quarterly revenue climbing 99% year over year to nearly $91.16 billion, equal to 64% of the top 10's combined sales.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Nvidia's share of top-10 fabless revenue is a key concentration metric to track quarter over quarter for AI-market breadth.

insights.claim: Nvidia's demand base broadened beyond hyperscale cloud providers to include NeoCloud operators, sovereign AI projects and enterprises.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Diversifying customer base reduces Nvidia's reliance on a handful of hyperscalers, a positive signal for revenue durability.
insights.locator: Demand broadened beyond hyperscale cloud providers

insights.claim: Broadcom held second place with revenue jumping 112% year over year to more than $18.89 billion, supported by custom AI silicon and networking products.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Broadcom's 112% growth outpaced even Nvidia's, underscoring custom ASIC/networking as a high-growth AI-adjacent segment worth tracking.
insights.locator: Broadcom held second place as revenue jumped 112%

insights.claim: AMD advanced to third place with revenue above $11.53 billion, which TrendForce linked to the growing importance of CPUs in agentic AI systems alongside continued share gains in x86 servers.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Agentic AI workloads are becoming a distinct CPU demand driver, a thesis to validate against AMD's server roadmap and share-gain trajectory.
insights.locator: AMD advanced to third with revenue above $11.53 billion

insights.claim: Qualcomm slipped to fourth place, earning more than $8.5 billion, as smartphone weakness and a smaller share of modems in Apple's newest iPhone offset continued automotive growth.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Loss of iPhone modem share is a concrete near-term headwind for Qualcomm that investors should weigh against its automotive diversification.
insights.locator: Qualcomm slipped to fourth, earning more than $8.5 billion

insights.claim: MediaTek placed fifth with about $4.81 billion in revenue, while Marvell ranked sixth at $2.63 billion as demand rose for 800G and 1.6T interconnect products.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Marvell's growth ties directly to AI-data-center interconnect upgrade cycles (800G/1.6T), a proxy for hyperscaler networking capex.
insights.locator: MediaTek placed fifth with about $4.81 billion

insights.claim: The remaining top-10 positions went to Realtek, Monolithic Power Systems, Novatek and OmniVision, which are pursuing growth in servers, AI power management, edge AI and optical communications respectively.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Smaller-cap fabless names are finding AI-adjacent niches (power management, edge AI, optical) worth monitoring for second-order AI capex beneficiaries.
insights.locator: The remaining positions went to Realtek

insights.claim: AMD's rise to third place signals a more diversified fabless market, but Nvidia's 64% share of top-10 revenue also reveals extreme concentration risk in AI semiconductor spending.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Despite broadening narratives, the AI chip market remains heavily single-vendor concentrated around Nvidia, a systemic risk for AI-infrastructure portfolios.
insights.quote: AMD's rise signals a more diversified market, but Nvidia's 64% share also reveals extreme concentration.
insights.locator: AMD's rise signals a more diversified market

insights.claim: For investors and supply-chain companies, the clearest opportunities increasingly sit with vendors tied to data-center infrastructure, while dependence on mature smartphone and PC markets remains a drag.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Direct investment framing: overweight data-center-linked fabless suppliers, underweight smartphone/PC-cycle-dependent names.
